title: Creation
summary: God creates the heavens and the earth, and makes humanity in his image.
dateNote: Placed at the start of the Genesis 5 genealogy; Scripture gives no date.

title: The Flood
summary: God judges a corrupt world by a flood and saves Noah, his family and the animals in the ark, then makes a covenant never to flood the earth again.
dateNote: 1,656 years after Creation by the Masoretic genealogies (Genesis 5; 7:6). The Septuagint and other readings give different totals.

title: The Tower of Babel
summary: People unite to build a tower to the heavens; God confuses their language and scatters them.
dateNote: Sometimes linked to the days of Peleg, "in whose days the earth was divided" (Genesis 10:25).

title: Birth of Abram
summary: Abram is born to Terah in Ur of the Chaldeans.

title: The call of Abram
summary: At 75, Abram obeys God's call to leave Haran for a land God will show him, with the promise that all nations will be blessed through him.

title: Abram in Egypt
summary: A famine drives Abram to Egypt, where he passes Sarai off as his sister and God protects her.

title: Abram and Lot part ways
summary: Their herds grow too large to share the land; Lot chooses the Jordan plain near Sodom and Abram settles at Hebron.

title: God's covenant with Abram
summary: God promises Abram offspring as many as the stars and confirms the promise of the land with a covenant ceremony.

title: Birth of Ishmael
summary: Hagar bears Abram a son, Ishmael, after God meets her in the wilderness.

title: Covenant of circumcision
summary: God renames Abram as Abraham and Sarai as Sarah, gives circumcision as the covenant sign, and promises a son within a year.

title: Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
summary: After Abraham pleads for the city, God rescues Lot and destroys Sodom and Gomorrah.

title: Birth of Isaac
summary: Sarah bears Isaac when Abraham is 100, just as God promised.

title: Abraham offers Isaac
summary: God tests Abraham by asking him to sacrifice Isaac on Mount Moriah, then provides a ram in his place.
dateNote: Isaac's age is not given; the date is an estimate.

title: Death of Sarah
summary: Sarah dies at 127; Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah, his first owned land in Canaan, to bury her.

title: Isaac marries Rebekah
summary: Abraham's servant finds Rebekah among Abraham's relatives near Haran, and she becomes Isaac's wife.

title: Birth of Jacob and Esau
summary: Rebekah bears twins; God says the older will serve the younger.

title: Death of Abraham
summary: Abraham dies at 175 and is buried by Isaac and Ishmael beside Sarah.

title: Jacob flees to Haran
summary: After taking Esau's blessing, Jacob flees to Laban and dreams of a stairway to heaven at Bethel.
dateNote: Estimated from Jacob's age at the move to Egypt and his years with Laban.

title: Jacob marries Leah and Rachel
summary: Jacob works fourteen years for Laban's daughters; his sons, the ancestors of Israel's tribes, are born in Haran.

title: Jacob wrestles with God
summary: Returning to Canaan, Jacob wrestles with God at Peniel, is renamed Israel, and is reconciled with Esau.

title: Joseph sold into slavery
summary: Jealous of their father's favorite, Joseph's brothers sell him to traders bound for Egypt.
dateNote: Joseph was 17 (Genesis 37:2).

title: Joseph rules in Egypt
summary: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams and is made second in command to prepare Egypt for seven years of famine.
dateNote: Joseph was 30 (Genesis 41:46).

title: Death of Isaac
summary: Isaac dies at 180 and is buried by Esau and Jacob.

title: Jacob's family moves to Egypt
summary: Joseph reveals himself to his brothers, and Jacob's household of seventy settles in Goshen.

title: Death of Jacob
summary: Jacob blesses his twelve sons and dies at 147; Joseph carries him back to be buried at Machpelah.

title: Death of Joseph
summary: Joseph dies at 110, making Israel promise to carry his bones to the Promised Land.

title: Israel enslaved in Egypt
summary: A new king who did not know Joseph forces the growing Israelite people into hard labor building store cities.
dateNote: Scripture does not date the start of the oppression; these spans are estimates.

title: Birth of Moses
summary: Hidden from Pharaoh's decree, the infant Moses is found in the Nile by Pharaoh's daughter and raised in the palace.

title: Moses flees to Midian
summary: After killing an Egyptian, Moses flees to Midian, marries Zipporah and tends Jethro's flocks for forty years.
dateNote: Moses was 40 (Acts 7:23).

title: The burning bush
summary: God appears to Moses in a bush that does not burn up, reveals his name, and sends him to bring Israel out of Egypt.

title: The ten plagues
summary: Pharaoh refuses to let Israel go, and God strikes Egypt with ten plagues.

title: The first Passover
summary: Israel marks its doorposts with the blood of a lamb, and the Lord passes over them when he strikes the firstborn of Egypt.
dateNote: The 14th day of the first month (Exodus 12:2, 6). Nisan falls in March–April.

title: The Exodus
summary: God brings Israel out of Egypt, leading them by a pillar of cloud and fire from Rameses through the sea to Mount Sinai.
description: Israel sets out from Rameses the day after Passover, about 600,000 men plus women and children (Exodus 12:37). God leads them not by the coastal road but through the wilderness toward the sea, where he parts the waters and destroys Pharaoh's army. They travel on through Marah, Elim and the wilderness of Sin, arriving at Mount Sinai in the third month.
dateNote: Early date (c. 1446 BC): 480 years before Solomon began the temple (1 Kings 6:1). Late date (c. 1260 BC): fits the city name Rameses (Exodus 1:11) and the reign of Rameses II.

title: Crossing the Red Sea
summary: God parts the sea, Israel crosses on dry ground, and the waters return over Pharaoh's chariots. Moses and Miriam lead a song of praise.

title: Manna and quail
summary: When Israel grumbles for food, God sends quail in the evening and bread from heaven each morning.

title: Battle with Amalek
summary: At Rephidim God gives water from the rock; Joshua defeats Amalek while Aaron and Hur hold up Moses' hands.

title: The covenant at Sinai
summary: At Mount Sinai God gives the Ten Commandments and makes his covenant with Israel as his treasured people.
dateNote: Israel arrived "on the third new moon" after leaving Egypt (Exodus 19:1).

title: The golden calf
summary: While Moses is on the mountain, the people make a golden calf; Moses intercedes and God renews the covenant.
dateNote: About forty days after Moses went up the mountain (Exodus 24:18).

title: The tabernacle is set up
summary: The tabernacle is raised and the glory of the Lord fills it.
dateNote: The first day of the first month of the second year (Exodus 40:17).

title: Israel leaves Sinai
summary: The cloud lifts from the tabernacle and Israel sets out by tribes toward the Promised Land.
dateNote: Numbers 10:11.

title: The twelve spies
summary: Ten spies bring a fearful report; only Joshua and Caleb trust God. Israel refuses to enter and is sentenced to forty years in the wilderness.
dateNote: "The time of the first ripe grapes" (Numbers 13:20), in summer.

title: Forty years in the wilderness
summary: The generation that refused to enter the land dies in the wilderness while God continues to provide for his people.

title: Death of Miriam
summary: Miriam dies and is buried at Kadesh.

title: Death of Aaron
summary: Aaron dies on Mount Hor at 123, and his son Eleazar becomes high priest.
dateNote: Numbers 33:38.

title: Journey to the Plains of Moab
summary: Israel travels around Edom, defeats Sihon and Og, and camps on the plains of Moab across from Jericho.

title: Death of Moses
summary: After giving his final words to Israel, Moses views the Promised Land from Mount Nebo and dies at 120. Joshua succeeds him.
dateNote: Moses spoke Deuteronomy in the 11th month of the 40th year (Deuteronomy 1:3).

title: Conquest of Canaan
summary: Joshua leads Israel across the Jordan and through campaigns in the center, south and north of Canaan, breaking the power of its kings.
dateNote: About seven years: Caleb was 40 when sent as a spy and 85 when the land was divided (Joshua 14:7–10).

title: Crossing the Jordan
summary: The Jordan stops flowing when the priests carrying the ark step into it, and Israel crosses into the Promised Land on dry ground.
dateNote: Joshua 4:19, forty years after the Exodus.

title: The fall of Jericho
summary: Israel marches around Jericho for seven days; at the trumpet blast and shout its walls fall. Rahab and her family are spared.

title: The sun stands still at Gibeon
summary: Joshua defends Gibeon against five Amorite kings, and the sun stands still until Israel has won.

title: The land divided among the tribes
summary: Joshua divides the land among the tribes by lot, and the tabernacle is set up at Shiloh.
dateNote: Caleb is 85, forty-five years after the spies (Joshua 14:7–10).

title: Joshua renews the covenant
summary: Near the end of his life Joshua gathers Israel at Shechem: "As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord." He dies at 110.

title: Deborah and Barak defeat Sisera
summary: At Deborah's word Barak leads ten thousand men from Mount Tabor; the Kishon sweeps away Sisera's chariots, and Jael kills Sisera.
dateNote: Dates in Judges are approximate: the book's periods of oppression and rest add up to more than the time available, so some probably overlapped.

title: Gideon defeats Midian
summary: God sends Gideon against the Midianite raiders with just three hundred men, armed with trumpets, jars and torches.
dateNote: Dates in Judges are approximate: the book's periods of oppression and rest add up to more than the time available, so some probably overlapped.

title: Ruth and Boaz
summary: Ruth the Moabite returns with Naomi to Bethlehem, gleans in Boaz's field, and marries him. Their son Obed is David's grandfather.
dateNote: Set "in the days when the judges ruled" (Ruth 1:1). Boaz is David's great-grandfather, which points to the late 1100s BC.

title: Birth of Samuel
summary: Hannah prays at Shiloh for a son; when Samuel is born she gives him to serve the Lord under Eli.

title: Samson fights the Philistines
summary: Samson, set apart from birth, fights the Philistines alone for twenty years, until Delilah betrays him; he dies pulling down the temple of Dagon at Gaza.
dateNote: He judged Israel twenty years (Judges 16:31), during the Philistine oppression that runs into Samuel's day. Dates in Judges are approximate: the book's periods of oppression and rest add up to more than the time available, so some probably overlapped.

title: The ark captured
summary: The Philistines defeat Israel at Aphek and capture the ark of the covenant. Eli's sons die in battle and Eli dies at the news.
dateNote: The ark then stays twenty years at Kiriath-jearim before Samuel gathers Israel at Mizpah (1 Samuel 7:2).

title: Saul becomes king
summary: Israel asks Samuel for a king like the other nations. God gives them Saul, whom Samuel anoints and the people acclaim.
dateNote: Acts 13:21 gives Saul forty years; the numbers in 1 Samuel 13:1 are damaged in the Hebrew text.

title: Samuel anoints David
summary: God rejects Saul and sends Samuel to Bethlehem, where he anoints Jesse's youngest son, the shepherd David.
dateNote: Not dated in Scripture; David is the youngest son, still keeping the sheep (1 Samuel 16:11).

title: David and Goliath
summary: The young David faces the Philistine champion Goliath with a sling and five stones, trusting the Lord, and kills him.
dateNote: Not dated in Scripture; David is still a youth (1 Samuel 17:33).

title: Death of Saul and Jonathan
summary: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa. Jonathan is killed and the wounded Saul falls on his own sword.

title: David's reign
summary: David rules seven and a half years from Hebron over Judah, then thirty-three years from Jerusalem over all Israel.
dateNote: Forty years in all (2 Samuel 5:4–5).

title: David takes Jerusalem
summary: David captures the Jebusite stronghold of Zion and makes Jerusalem his capital, then brings the ark there.
dateNote: After seven and a half years reigning in Hebron (2 Samuel 5:5).

title: God's covenant with David
summary: Through Nathan, God promises David a house and a kingdom that will last forever: a promise the New Testament sees fulfilled in Jesus.
dateNote: Not dated; it comes once David is settled in his palace in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 7:1).

title: David and Bathsheba
summary: David takes Bathsheba and has her husband Uriah killed. Nathan confronts him, and David repents (Psalm 51), but trouble follows his house.
dateNote: Not dated; it happens while Israel's army besieges Rabbah of the Ammonites (2 Samuel 11:1).

title: Solomon's reign
summary: Solomon asks God for wisdom, rules Israel at the height of its wealth and peace, and builds the temple, but his many foreign wives turn his heart to other gods.
dateNote: Forty years (1 Kings 11:42).

title: Solomon builds the temple
summary: Solomon builds the house of the Lord on Mount Moriah; at its dedication God's glory fills the temple.
dateNote: Begun in Solomon's fourth year, 480 years after the Exodus (1 Kings 6:1), and finished seven years later (1 Kings 6:37–38).

title: The kingdom divides
summary: When Rehoboam refuses to lighten Solomon's heavy demands, the ten northern tribes make Jeroboam king. Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
summary: After three years of drought Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal. God answers with fire from heaven, then sends rain.
dateNote: During Ahab's reign (874–853 BC); the year isn't given.

title: Elijah taken up to heaven
summary: Elijah parts the Jordan and is taken up in a whirlwind as chariots of fire appear. Elisha takes up his cloak and his ministry.
dateNote: Not dated; Elisha is already prophet while Jehoshaphat still reigns in Judah (2 Kings 3), before about 848 BC.

title: Jonah preaches to Nineveh
summary: Jonah runs from God's call, is swallowed by a great fish, and finally warns Nineveh, which repents and is spared.
dateNote: Jonah prophesied under Jeroboam II of Israel (793–753 BC, 2 Kings 14:25); the year of his mission isn't given.

title: Amos warns Israel
summary: A shepherd from Judah denounces the northern kingdom's injustice and hollow worship at Bethel, and foretells its fall.
dateNote: "Two years before the earthquake," under Uzziah and Jeroboam II (Amos 1:1), about 760 BC.

title: Isaiah's ministry
summary: Called in a vision of God's holiness, Isaiah counsels Judah's kings, warns of judgment and promises a coming king and a suffering servant.
dateNote: From the year King Uzziah died, about 740 BC (Isaiah 6:1), into Hezekiah's reign and perhaps beyond: Isaiah records Sennacherib's death in 681 BC (Isaiah 37:38).

title: Fall of Samaria
summary: After a three-year siege Assyria takes Samaria and deports the people of the northern kingdom. Israel's ten tribes are scattered.
dateNote: Assyrian records credit the conquest to Shalmaneser V and Sargon II; Thiele dates it 723/722 BC.

title: Sennacherib threatens Jerusalem
summary: Assyria's king takes Lachish and surrounds Jerusalem. Hezekiah prays, Isaiah promises deliverance, and the angel of the Lord strikes the Assyrian camp.
dateNote: Sennacherib's own annals and the reliefs of Lachish from his palace record this campaign of 701 BC.

title: Josiah's reform
summary: The Book of the Law is found in the temple. Josiah renews the covenant, destroys the idols and celebrates the Passover.
dateNote: In Josiah's eighteenth year (2 Kings 22:3).

title: Jeremiah's ministry
summary: For four decades Jeremiah warns Judah to repent and submit to Babylon, weeps over Jerusalem's fall, and promises a new covenant.
dateNote: From Josiah's thirteenth year (Jeremiah 1:2) until after Jerusalem fell, when he was taken to Egypt (Jeremiah 43). The end date is estimated.

title: Daniel taken to Babylon
summary: Nebuchadnezzar takes young nobles from Jerusalem to serve in his court, among them Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.
dateNote: In the third year of Jehoiakim (Daniel 1:1), when Nebuchadnezzar first took Jerusalem in 605 BC.

title: King Jehoiachin taken to Babylon
summary: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem, carries King Jehoiachin and ten thousand leading citizens to Babylon, among them the priest Ezekiel, and makes Zedekiah king.
dateNote: The Babylonian Chronicle dates the city's capture to 2 Adar (16 March 597 BC).

title: Fall of Jerusalem
summary: Babylon besieges Jerusalem for a year and a half, breaks through the walls, burns the temple and takes the people into exile.
dateNote: From the start of the siege (2 Kings 25:1) to the burning of the temple (Jeremiah 52:12). Thiele dates the fall to 586 BC; others to 587.
